Hi, I'm Yana!

Postdoctoral Scholar Research Associate at Caltech · Amelia Earhart Fellow

Aerospace & Control Engineer · Oxford DPhil · Cambridge MEng & BA (Engineering)

  • Download CV (PDF)
  • lishkova@caltech.edu
  • Google Scholar
  • LinkedIn
  • GitHub

I'm a postdoctoral researcher in the AMBER Lab at Caltech, working with Prof. Aaron Ames and collaborating closely with Prof. Joel Burdick's group. I develop safe, autonomous guidance and control for spacecraft and robots, combining optimization-based control with formal guarantees, safety filters, and structure-preserving methods for nonlinear dynamics. My work spans theory, simulation, and experimental validation, from Mars helicopter simulations to software- and hardware-in-the-loop (SIL/HIL) testing on spacecraft free-flyers and quadrotors. I also co-lead the lab's spacecraft robotics testbed and supervise students working on these platforms.

Before Caltech, I completed my DPhil (PhD) in the Oxford Control Group with Prof. Mark Cannon and Prof. Sina Ober-Blöbaum, followed by an EPSRC Doctoral Prize fellowship on spacecraft trajectory design. At Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories (MERL), I worked on divert-feasible lunar landing under navigation uncertainty, with a patent now pending. I hold a BA and MEng from Cambridge, specialising in aerospace and control engineering, and a technical diploma from Edinburgh, having begun my education at a mathematics high school in Bulgaria.

Alongside research, I've been involved in teaching, student welfare, and STEM outreach. I've received two EPSRC grants, a 2022 Amelia Earhart Fellowship, and a 2023 Royal Aeronautical Society (RAeS) commendation for outreach. Outside the lab, I fly gliders, have helped build amateur rockets, and love organising events, from scientific seminars to college May Balls.

What I work on

Spacecraft autonomy, guidance and controlRead more →
Optimization-based guidance and control for spacecraft, from multi-agent close-proximity operations and flexible or tethered spacecraft to planetary landing, with robust and probabilistic safety guarantees.
Safe exploration and landing with contingenciesRead more →
Contingency-aware decision-making built on control barrier functions (CBFs), Hamilton–Jacobi reachability and safe stochastic controllability sets, keeping safe options available when plans go wrong, from lunar landing with feasible divert sites to Mars helicopter exploration and robot teams recovering from failures.
Robust and nonlinear optimization-based controlRead more →
Robust model predictive control (MPC) and nonlinear trajectory optimization via convexification, including lossless convexification and difference-of-convex methods, with guarantees of feasibility, stability, robustness and convergence.
Structure-preserving numerical methodsRead more →
Variational multirate integrators and optimal control numerical methods that preserve key physical properties, such as momentum and energy behaviour, when the dynamics are discretized, for accurate and efficient simulation and control of systems with coupled slow and fast nonlinear dynamics.
From algorithms to hardwareRead more →
Software-in-the-loop (SIL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) validation on ATMOS air-bearing free-flyers and Crazyflie quadrotors in the AMBER Lab.

Projects

All projects
  • NewDemonstration video after review

    Fault-tolerant connectivity for multi-robot swarms

    When a robot fails, matrix control barrier functions restore the team's resilient connectivity by moving only the affected subgroups. Tested with Crazyflie quadrotors.

    Caltech, under review at ICRA 2027

  • NewDemonstration video after review

    Robust trajectory optimization for 6DOF spacecraft on an air-bearing testbed

    Robust MPC for coupled translation and rotation, validated on an ATMOS robotic free-flyer.

    Caltech, under review at ICRA 2027

  • Contingency-aware exploration for Mars helicopters

    Exploring unmapped terrain while always keeping a safe landing zone within reach.

    Caltech, in progress

  • Certified deadline-aware contingency landing

    Chained LQR funnels that certify a vehicle can still reach enough landing sites before a deadline.

    Caltech, in preparation

  • Steering with Contingencies: Combinatorial Stabilization and Reach-Avoid Filters

    Safety filters that steer to a nominal target while keeping a chosen number of alternative targets reachable.

    Caltech and UC San Diego, CDC 2026

  • Divert-feasible lunar landing

    Convex landing trajectories that keep safe divert options open under navigation uncertainty. Patent pending.

    MERL, CDC 2024

  • ATMOS free-flyer testbed

    Air-bearing free-flyers that mimic frictionless motion in orbit, taking our controllers from PX4 simulation to hardware.

    Caltech AMBER Lab, 2025 to present

  • Difference-of-convex MPC

    My approach to trajectory optimization and MPC for nonlinear systems, with feasibility, stability and convergence guarantees under disturbances.

    Oxford, IEEE TAC 2025

  • Multirate structure-preserving control

    Variational integrators and MPC that treat fast and slow dynamics at their own rates, applied to flexible spacecraft.

    Oxford DPhil

Testbeds

The robots we take our algorithms to, and the projects that run on them.

  • ATMOS free-flyer testbed

    Caltech AMBER Lab, co-lead, 2025 to present

    Air-bearing free-flyers that mimic spacecraft with near-frictionless planar motion, running PX4 and ROS 2 for software- and hardware-in-the-loop (SIL/HIL) testing.

    Projects on this testbed: Robust trajectory optimization for 6DOF spacecraft on an air-bearing testbed, Safe multi-agent close-proximity operations

    ATMOS platform The students who built it

  • Crazyflie quadrotor testbed

    Caltech AMBER Lab

    Small quadrotors for multi-robot experiments, from hardware-in-the-loop runs to flights with the full team.

    Projects on this testbed: Fault-tolerant connectivity for multi-robot swarms, Certified deadline-aware contingency landing via chained LQR funnels (in progress)

Spacecraft autonomy, guidance and control

Guidance and control with robust and probabilistic guarantees, tested on air-bearing free-flyers.

  • Demonstration video to appear after review

    Robust trajectory optimization for 6DOF spacecraft on an air-bearing testbed (placeholder title) New

    Caltech, under review at ICRA 2027, with SURF student Deepak G

    An exact difference-of-convex decomposition of coupled translational and attitude spacecraft dynamics, enabling convex-optimization-based MPC that controls position and attitude together, validated on an ATMOS free-flyer.

    Paper (ICRA 2027, under review) Paper and demonstration video to appear after the review process

  • Safe multi-agent spacecraft close-proximity operations In progress

    Caltech, AFOSR-funded, project co-lead

    Safe guidance and control for multiple spacecraft operating in close proximity, tested on our ATMOS free-flyers.

  • Optimal control of flexible spacecraft

    DPhil, Oxford

    Simultaneous slewing and vibration control of flexible spacecraft. The optimal control problem is discretized on coupled micro and macro time grids with a multirate variational approach, matching single-rate accuracy at a lower computational cost.

    Paper 1 (AAS 2020) Paper 2 (GAMM 2024) Paper 3 (IFAC 2026)

    Slides (AAS 2020) Slides (IFAC 2026)

    Talk video (AAS 2020)

  • Electrodynamic tethers in a three-body environment

    With Kyushu University

    A structure-preserving variational model of 6DOF spacecraft motion in the three-body problem with electrodynamic tether forcing, including a multirate version that reduces computational cost. We use it to design optimal transfers controlled only through attitude torques.

    Paper (IAC 2023)

  • Optimal maneuver planning for small satellites in LEO

    Master's thesis of Ralitsa Velikova, Sofia University St. Kliment Ohridski, co-mentored

    Planning fuel-efficient orbital maneuvers for small satellites in low Earth orbit.

Model predictive control

Control that plans ahead and replans as it goes, with guarantees.

  • Difference-of-convex MPC with guarantees

    DPhil, Oxford, with Prof. Mark Cannon

    Trajectory optimization and MPC for nonlinear systems with feasibility, stability and convergence guarantees that hold under disturbances.

    Paper 1 (IEEE TAC 2025) Paper 2 (CDC 2023)

  • Multirate variational nonlinear MPC

    Also in Structure-preserving simulation and control

    DPhil, Oxford, ECC 2022

    Nonlinear MPC built on a multirate variational integrator, which discretizes slow and fast dynamics at their own rates while preserving the physics. This allows larger prediction time steps, reducing computation with guaranteed recursive feasibility.

    Paper (ECC 2022)

    Slides (ECC 2022)

  • Tutorial: robust data-driven MPC with difference-of-convex functions

    Invited tutorial, ACC 2025 workshop, with Prof. Mark Cannon

    A tutorial on using difference-of-convex representations, including learned ones, for robust MPC.

    Slides (ACC 2025 tutorial, my part)

Structure-preserving simulation and control

Numerical methods that keep the physics. The core of my DPhil.

  • Multirate simulation and optimal control

    DPhil, Oxford, with S. Ober-Blöbaum, M. Cannon and S. Leyendecker

    A structure-preserving variational approach to the simulation and optimal control of systems whose dynamics evolve on different time scales.

    Paper 1 (AAS 2020) Paper 2 (GAMM 2024) Paper 3 (journal, ready for submission)

    Slides (AAS 2020)

    Talk video (AAS 2020)

  • Multirate variational nonlinear MPC

    Also in Model predictive control

    DPhil, Oxford, ECC 2022

    Nonlinear MPC built on a multirate variational integrator, which discretizes slow and fast dynamics at their own rates while preserving the physics. This allows larger prediction time steps, reducing computation with guaranteed recursive feasibility.

    Paper (ECC 2022)

    Slides (ECC 2022)

  • Discrete Lagrangian neural networks

    Also in Learning dynamical models

    With Cambridge and Paderborn

    Learning a discrete Lagrangian and its symmetry group directly from observed motion. The variational structure keeps simulations physically consistent, the discovered symmetries reveal conserved quantities such as momentum, and predictions improve even from noisy position data alone.

    Paper (IFAC 2023)

    Slides (IFAC 2023)

Learning dynamical models

Learned models with structure that control can use.

  • Discrete Lagrangian neural networks

    Also in Structure-preserving simulation and control

    With Cambridge and Paderborn

    Learning a discrete Lagrangian and its symmetry group directly from observed motion. The variational structure keeps simulations physically consistent, the discovered symmetries reveal conserved quantities such as momentum, and predictions improve even from noisy position data alone.

    Paper (IFAC 2023)

    Slides (IFAC 2023)

  • Difference-of-convex neural networks for spacecraft 6DOF control In progress

    University of Oxford (EPSRC Doctoral Prize funding) and Caltech

    Neural network models of spacecraft dynamics in difference-of-convex form, for direct use in robust tube-based MPC of full 6DOF motion.

Theses and earlier projects

  • DPhil thesis: Simulation, optimisation, and control of multirate dynamics

    University of Oxford, 2024, supervised by Prof. Mark Cannon and Prof. Sina Ober-Blöbaum, examined by Prof. Moritz Diehl and Prof. Paul Goulart

    Structure-preserving multirate variational methods for the simulation and optimal control of systems with dynamics on different time scales, applied to flexible satellites and 6DOF spacecraft in the three-body problem. Building on these, successive convex approximation MPC schemes with guarantees of recursive feasibility and stability, including robustness to disturbances and convergence to a local optimum.

    Thesis (ORA)

  • MEng thesis: Adjoint-based optimization of hydrofoils

    University of Cambridge, 2019, supervised by Prof. Matthew Juniper

    Three flow solvers in Fortran 90, comparing finite differences with forward and reverse automatic differentiation for aerofoil shape optimization.

    Thesis (PDF)

  • Martlet 3 rocket

    Cambridge University Spaceflight, Black Rock Desert, Nevada, 2017

    A boosted-dart rocket built to break the UK amateur altitude record. The motor exploded at Mach 1.2, but the dart flew on to 3.5 km and was recovered under parachute.

    About CUSF

Community contributions

Groups that shaped me, and the roles I took on in them.

  • Royal Aeronautical SocietyOxford Branch

    2022 to 2024

    Royal Aeronautical Society (RAeS)

    The UK-based professional body for the global aerospace community. As the Oxford Branch's Young Person Representative, I helped shape how the branch engages students and early-career engineers. In 2023 the Society awarded me its Young Person's Achievement Commendation for this work.

    My role: Young Person Representative, Oxford Branch committee

    aerosociety.com 2023 Commendation

  • 2021 to 2023

    Graduate Joint Consultative Committee

    I chaired and revived the Graduate Joint Consultative Committee. We secured a departmental budget and made a student representative compulsory on departmental panels. We launched a student information website, improved workspaces and ran events, including a "How to complete your DPhil" talk with the Director of Graduate Studies. I also represented graduate students on the department's Graduate Studies Committee and the MPLS Division's Graduate Joint Consultative Forum, taking up student cases and advising on policy.

    My role: GJCC Chair, 2022 and 2023 (Graduate Student Body President)

    I am a 2022 Amelia Earhart Fellow, part of Zonta International's global network of women in aerospace engineering and space sciences.

    Oxford University Gliding Club

    The university club flies with the Oxford Gliding Club at RAF Weston-on-the-Green, where members learn from scratch and can fly solo within months.
